record.narrative: I register a first discovery set that prioritizes complete binary predictors and outcomes with informative scale and variance. More negative CRISPR dependency scores indicate stronger dependency, so negative-direction claims hypothesize stronger dependency in the exposed group, while positive-direction claims hypothesize weaker dependency. The main-effect set samples several outcome distributions and prevalence strata, and the interaction set tests whether a biomarker's association with dependency is context-dependent across common co-occurring states. All initial claims are unresolved pending 95 percent Welch intervals and evaluation against the 10 percent relative-difference threshold. Plausible alternatives for every registered comparison are no association or the opposite sign because the labels are opaque and the dependency outcomes may reflect distinct genetic or cellular contexts.

I request analyses for all twelve registered first-wave comparisons. This maximizes discovery coverage while the dataset is fresh: ten main effects spanning multiple dependency scores and common binary predictors, plus two complementary interaction tests for shared feature_002/feature_034 structure. All comparison cells should be adequately populated by the prevalence pattern, and the registered directions and initial unresolved assessments are retained for evidence-based appraisal.

I assessed all twelve discovery comparisons using their signed 95% Welch intervals and the 10% clinically significant relative-difference benchmark. Because the estimates are already signed to each hypothesis direction, a positive estimate supports the directional claim and a negative estimate supports the opposite contrast. None of the claims reached an acceptable accept level: no estimate clearly exceeded 10%, and no interval provided both statistical direction support and a clinically meaningful lower bound. The first-wave set therefore does not yet establish any predictor or interaction effect meeting the scientific bar. I rejected the comparisons where the signed interval gave little support for even a 10% effect in the claimed direction and closed them: H1, H7, H8, H9, and H10. I kept several wide or borderline results unresolved rather than rejecting them, because their intervals can still include clinically meaningful effects: H2, H3, H5, H6, H11, H12, and especially H4. H4 is active because feature_034 on outcome_013 has a positive signed estimate approaching the clinical threshold and an interval that just crosses zero; it is the strongest candidate in this wave, though not accepted. H12 is also active because the feature_034 by feature_002 interaction on outcome_014 has a large positive signed point estimate, but the interval is very wide and includes zero, so it remains hypothesis-generating. I deliberately requested no validation: independent validation is not useful yet because no claim demonstrates a stable clinically meaningful effect, and validating borderline nulls would widen independent intervals without improving confidence. Plausible competing explanations include confounding by correlated predictor states, outcome-specific genetic context, and the instability of relative differences when the comparator mean is near zero, which makes outcome_006 and outcome_014 especially sensitive to scale. I did not use constant or high-cardinality predictors such as feature_033, feature_049, or feature_003, avoiding trivial or leakage-prone comparisons. The next wave focuses on a follow-up of the H4/H12 signal and broad but stable exploration of complete binary predictors across additional dependency outcomes.

No independent validation result and no response deadline are currently pending, so there is no new validation evidence to integrate. The present supported findings are limited: the accepted claim set is empty, and no discovery comparison has yet provided robust evidence of a clinically meaningful relative difference in a dependency score. The five closed comparisons are negative findings in this dataset: H1, H7, H8, H9, and H10 give little interval support for the hypothesized 10% or larger relative difference in the claimed direction. H2, H3, H5, H6, and H11 remain unresolved but deferred because their point estimates are near zero or their intervals are too broad to establish either a clinically meaningful effect or a useful negative conclusion. The strongest unresolved leads are H4 and H12. H4, the feature_034 effect on outcome_013, has a signed estimate just below the clinical threshold and a 95% interval that narrowly crosses zero; it is promising but cannot yet be accepted. H12, the feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction on outcome_014, has a larger point estimate but a very wide interval that includes zero, making it hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. These conclusions are strictly dataset associations, not causal claims and not necessarily generalizable. The most informative next analysis remains the focused follow-up of the feature_034 signal: H13 tests the outcome_013 effect within feature_002=1, H14 tests the main feature_034 effect on outcome_014, and H12 plus the new H25 test whether feature_002 modifies the feature_034 association. The broad binary screens H15 through H24 remain useful for discovery, but priority should remain on the feature_034 leads until an interval robustly excludes the null while meeting the 10% relative-difference benchmark; only then should independent validation be requested.

The strongest existing signals are still feature_034's positive association with outcome_013 and the feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction for outcome_014. I therefore register focused follow-ups that test whether the feature_034 association is homogeneous, concentrated in feature_002=1, or broad across outcomes. Direct subgroup mean differences complement H13, H14, H25, and H12: the new outcome_013 and outcome_014 subgroup tests can reveal whether the large interaction estimate is driven by a clinically meaningful effect within feature_002=1 and whether the complement remains null. The outcome_006 subgroup test is motivated by outcome_006 and outcome_014 having similarly near-zero dependency-score distributions and by the outcome_014 interaction lead. I also register several feature_034 main effects on related but previously untested dependency scores with stable negative means, where a positive shift denotes weaker dependency. These cross-outcome tests can distinguish a context-specific association from a broader marker association. All comparisons use common binary states with expected cell counts well above 20. The claims are registered as unresolved and directional, not accepted, because prior intervals do not yet robustly exclude the null while meeting the 10% relative-difference benchmark. I did not propose validation yet because no claim has clinically compelling interval support; a focused feature_034 wave should decide whether validation is warranted. Plausible alternatives remain no association, an opposite sign, confounding by correlated predictor states, or outcome-specific genetic context. These are dataset associations only and not causal or generalizable claims.

I allocate the second wave primarily to testing the unresolved feature_034 leads. H13 directly tests the outcome_013 feature_034 effect within feature_002=1, while H25 tests whether that effect differs from the complement; together they localize and test modification of the H4 signal. H14 tests the overall feature_034 effect on outcome_014, and H27 and H28 decompose that effect within feature_002=1 and feature_002=0 to interpret the wide H12 interaction. H29 extends the near-zero outcome_014/feature_002 context to outcome_006, another distribution with a near-zero mean where relative effects require careful interpretation. To distinguish a context-specific marker association from broader dependency-score associations, H30 through H33 test feature_034 main effects on outcome_008, outcome_011, outcome_012, and outcome_002. H15 and H19 add two untested complete binary predictors on different outcomes to maintain broad discovery coverage. H26 is deferred as a duplicate of H13 rather than analyzed separately. All estimates will be interpreted as signed to the hypothesis direction; acceptance will require clinically meaningful support near or beyond the 10% relative-difference benchmark and an interval that supports the claimed direction. These analyses remain dataset-conditional associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

I assessed the second discovery wave using signed 95% Welch intervals and the 10% relative-difference benchmark, interpreting each estimate in the direction of its registered claim. The feature_034 lead remains not robust. H13 supports a positive outcome_013 association within feature_002=1, but its point estimate is well below the approximate clinical threshold and the interval crosses zero. H25's negative signed interaction estimate does not support positive modification by feature_002=1; combined with H13 it suggests that the overall H4 signal may instead be concentrated in the feature_002=0 complement, motivating a direct f002=0 outcome_013 test rather than validation of H4 or H25. For outcome_014, H14 gives little evidence for an overall positive feature_034 effect and is closed, while H27 and H28 reveal a possible context split: positive within feature_002=1 and negative within feature_002=0. H27 is the most promising context-specific lead, but it is not acceptable because the interval crosses zero and the near-zero outcome scale makes relative effects unstable. H28, as a positive claim, is rejected; I propose a reversed f002=0 claim to test the observed negative direction. H29 is too wide and near-null to prioritize. The cross-outcome feature_034 tests H30 through H33 do not support a broader positive dependency-shift effect and are closed. Broad tests H15 and H19 remain deferred because their estimates are small or imprecise. I request no validation: no claim yet has an interval that robustly excludes zero while meeting the clinical threshold, and validating unstable near-zero effects would be premature. Competing explanations include outcome-specific genetic context, confounding by correlated states, random interaction noise from multiple comparisons, and scale instability for outcomes with means near zero.

No independent validation response and no validation deadline are pending, so the current synthesis is based entirely on discovery evidence in this dataset. The accepted claim set remains empty. The most defensible current conclusions are negative or provisional. The closed comparisons H1, H7, H8, H9, H10, H14, H28, H30, H31, H32, and H33 are negative findings in this dataset: their signed estimates and 95% intervals do not support a clinically meaningful 10% or larger relative effect in the claimed direction. H14 and H28 also argue against a broad positive feature_034 association with outcome_014 or with outcome_014 specifically when feature_002 equals 0. The strongest unresolved lead is feature_034 on outcome_013, H4, but it should not be accepted: its signed point estimate is about 0.0187 on an outcome_013 scale of approximately -0.269, which is roughly a 7% relative difference, below the 10% clinical benchmark, and its interval still crosses zero. Its subgroup localization remains unresolved: H13 is positive within feature_002 equals 1 but small and imprecise, while H25 does not support positive modification by feature_002 equals 1. This motivates the pending direct test H34 within feature_002 equals 0. For outcome_014, H12 and H27 suggest a possible context-specific positive feature_034 shift within feature_002 equals 1, and H35 suggests a possible negative shift within feature_002 equals 0, but all intervals are wide, cross null, and involve a near-zero outcome mean where relative differences are unstable. Therefore these are hypothesis-generating, not accepted. I do not treat H35 as independently confirming H28's reversed direction because it is derived from the same subgroup contrast. The broad deferred comparisons are similarly too imprecise to support acceptance. The most informative next analysis is to complete the feature_034 localization with H34 and H36, which tests whether feature_002 itself has an outcome_013 association that could explain conditional contrasts, while simultaneously running the untested broad binary screens H16 through H24 and the new broad screen H37. A feature_034 claim should be considered for validation only if the direct subgroup or main-effect estimate reaches a clinically meaningful relative effect, roughly 0.027 or larger on the outcome_013 scale, with interval support excluding the null. Otherwise the evidence supports only dataset-specific negative findings and unresolved hypothesis-generating signals, not causal or generalizable conclusions.

There is no new validation response to integrate, and the accepted claim set remains empty. I therefore add focused refinements of the current feature_034 lead and one common categorical screen. First, H25 was registered with a positive interaction direction but its signed evidence is negative, indicating that any positive outcome_013 effect of feature_034 may be attenuated rather than amplified when feature_002 equals 1. I propose a reversed interaction claim to test that observed direction explicitly: the raw feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction is negative in the outcome_013 comparison. This does not validate the overall H4 association; it localizes the modification signal and remains dataset specific. Second, I register a main effect of the balanced complete binary predictor feature_060 on outcome_013. This fills a gap because feature_060 has been tested on outcome_008 and outcome_011 but not on the most informative outcome_013. The registered positive direction corresponds to weaker dependency, but the expected raw contrast is uncertain. Third, I register the common two-level categorical predictor feature_054, comparing level_002 with the majority level_001, also on outcome_013. This adds diversity beyond the feature_034/feature_002 family and uses a predictor with approximately 578 versus 1422 observations, likely satisfying cell-size rules. The registered negative direction corresponds to stronger dependency, but the expected raw contrast is uncertain. For outcome_013, a 10% relative difference is roughly an absolute shift of 0.027 on the observed mean scale, and any accepted conclusion should require an interval supporting a clinically meaningful effect, not merely a nominal interval away from zero. Plausible alternatives for all new claims include no association, an effect in the opposite direction, confounding by correlated predictor states, or outcome-specific genetic context. These are observational associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability. I also closed redundant duplicate H26 and deferred low-priority evidence-backed comparisons H19 and H29 to keep follow-up focused on the pending feature_034 localization and the most informative broad screens.

I request the twelve currently most informative untested or localization-critical comparisons. The priority is the feature_034/outcome_013 lead: H34 directly tests the feature_034 association within feature_002=0, completing the subgroup decomposition after H13 tested feature_002=1; H36 tests the marginal feature_002 association on outcome_013, which helps distinguish a true modification pattern from differential baseline means; H39 and H40 add two broad complete or common categorical predictors on outcome_013. The remaining requests are untested complete binary screens spanning other dependency outcomes, selected to maximize outcome and predictor diversity: H16, H17, H20, H21, H22, H23, H24, and H37. I omit redundant claims such as H26/H38/H35 analyses whose evidence is already available, and omit H18 because it duplicates outcome_004 coverage when H37 is also included. All estimates will be interpreted as signed to the claim direction; acceptance will require evidence near or beyond a 10% relative difference with uncertainty compatible with a clinically meaningful effect, while outcomes with near-zero means will be judged cautiously. These remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims.

I assessed the 12 new discovery results using signed 95% Welch intervals, valid-cell diagnostics, and a 10% relative-effect benchmark approximated from the absolute mean scale of each outcome. The strongest candidate is H34: feature_034 exposure within feature_002=0 has a signed estimate of about 0.025 on outcome_013, close to the approximate 0.027 absolute benchmark for 10% of the outcome_013 mean magnitude, but its interval still includes zero and crosses slightly into the null. I therefore keep H34 unresolved and active rather than accepting it. Because it is the best borderline localization of the earlier H4 signal, I request independent validation of H34 only if the claim can withstand multiplicity-adjusted independent evidence; validation does not imply acceptance.

Most new broad screens are negative for clinically meaningful effects in the claimed direction. H36, H39, H16, H17, H20, H23, and H37 have signed interval upper bounds below the approximate 10% absolute benchmark, so they do not support a clinically meaningful claimed difference and are rejected/closed. H36 also rules out a meaningful marginal feature_002 association on outcome_013, which makes the H13/H34 split more consistent with differential conditional feature_034 effects rather than a simple feature_002 main effect.

H40, H21, H22, and H24 remain unresolved because their upper confidence bounds cross the approximate clinical threshold, although their point estimates are small and the intervals are too imprecise for acceptance. I defer these low-priority screens rather than closing them completely. The new results do not establish causality or generalizability. Competing explanations for the remaining H34 lead include chance subgroup finding, correlated predictors, confounding by unobserved genetic context, outcome-specific behavior, or a real weaker-dependency shift in the feature_002=0 context. To broaden beyond binary predictors, I also registered nominal multi-level categorical comparisons on stable outcomes. These directions are exploratory because level labels are opaque; they mainly test whether any categorical level shows a clinically meaningful dependency-score shift.

The independent validation results materially change the interpretation of the feature_034 leads. For H34, the outcome_013 feature_034 effect within feature_002=0 was borderline in discovery (R25: +0.0250, 95% CI -0.0023 to +0.0523), close to but not clearly at the approximate 10% absolute benchmark of about 0.027 on the outcome_013 scale. The independent validation result was essentially null (R37: +0.0005, adjusted CI -0.0392 to +0.0402, alpha about 0.0038). Because the validation interval includes zero and the point estimate is far below the clinical benchmark, I reject H34 as a clinically meaningful positive association in this dataset. This closes the subgroup-specific feature_034/feature_002=0 hypothesis on outcome_013.

For H28, the validation creates inconsistency rather than support. The original discovery estimate for positive feature_034 effect within feature_002=0 on outcome_014 was negative (R17 raw contrast negative relative to the positive claim), whereas the independent validation estimate is positive and large in magnitude (R38: +0.0421, adjusted CI -0.0249 to +0.1090). The validation point exceeds the approximate 10% benchmark for outcome_014, but the interval still includes null and the direction is not consistent across samples. Since outcome_014 has a near-zero mean, relative-effect inference is especially unstable. I therefore reopen H28 as unresolved and defer it rather than accepting or finally rejecting it. The same validation contrast also leaves the reversed claim H35 uncertain, so I defer H35 as well.

Given that H34 failed validation, I down-weight the original overall feature_034/outcome_013 lead H4. I do not reject H4 outright because its discovery interval upper bound still allows a clinically meaningful positive shift, but I defer it because the strongest localized version failed independent validation. The accepted set remains empty. Current negative findings include H1, H7, H8, H9, H10, H14, H16, H17, H20, H23, H30, H31, H32, H33, H36, H37, H39, and now H34, none of which support a clinically meaningful effect in the claimed direction. The most informative next analyses are the registered broad multi-level categorical screens H41-H47, especially on outcome_013, plus H18 if capacity permits, rather than continued feature_034/feature_002 follow-up. These conclusions are dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

With no due validation response and no accepted claims, I propose new discovery comparisons rather than more feature_034/feature_002 follow-up. The strongest previous outcome_013 localization, H34, failed independent validation, and the outcome_014 validation response was directionally inconsistent with discovery and is unstable because outcome_014's mean is close to zero. Therefore I deprioritize that predictor family and broaden to nominal categorical contrasts and untested complete binary predictors. The registered H41-H47 categorical screens each test one level contrast; I add complementary contrasts on outcome_013 because multi-level labels are nominal and a meaningful association may appear in any contrast against the dominant level. I also register feature_008 and feature_042, two complete binary predictors with favorable prevalence, to increase power relative to very rare binary predictors. Additional lower-prevalence binary screens add diversity across dependency outcomes. I set direction +1 for these new comparisons to make the reported signed estimate equal to the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast; if an opposite result is clinically meaningful, it can be converted into a reversed claim. The anticipated raw direction is uncertain because predictor level labels are opaque. For outcome_013, the 10% relative benchmark corresponds roughly to an absolute shift of about 0.027 on the observed mean scale, so acceptance will require both a sufficiently large point estimate and uncertainty compatible with that magnitude. These proposals remain dataset-specific association tests, not causal or generalizable conclusions.

I request the 12 most informative currently untested broad-screen claims. The feature_034/feature_002 family is deprioritized after the subgroup-specific outcome_013 lead H34 failed independent validation and the outcome_014 validation contrast was inconsistent and unstable because outcome_014 has a near-zero mean. Therefore I focus on the registered categorical screens H41-H47 plus H18 to cover outcome_013, outcome_002, outcome_003, outcome_004, outcome_007, outcome_009, and several multi-level predictors. I add the high-prevalence complete binary predictors feature_008 and feature_042 on outcome_013 (H55, H56) and on additional stable dependency outcomes (H57, H58) because their cell sizes are expected to be adequate and they provide more precise tests than very rare binary predictors. These 12 comparisons maximize diversity across predictors and outcomes while avoiding further feature_034 follow-up unless a new signal appears. If any categorical cell has fewer than 20 observations, that result should be treated as diagnostic invalid rather than evidence. All reported estimates will be interpreted as signed to the claim direction and judged against the approximately 10% absolute-effect benchmark for each outcome, not merely by zero exclusion.

The 12 new discovery results are mostly null or imprecise for the claimed directional effects, but one comparison is a strong signal in the opposite direction. H45 tested outcome_007 for feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 with direction +1. The signed estimate is -0.0503, with 95% Welch interval [-0.0788, -0.0218] and valid cells 175/1440. Because the registered direction is positive, this result does not support H45 as a positive association and is therefore rejected as a positive claim. However, the raw contrast is large and negative: outcome_007 is about 0.050 lower in level_001 than level_003, approximately 20% of the absolute outcome_007 mean. The interval excludes zero, and its lower magnitude is close to the 10% clinical benchmark, although the upper magnitude is slightly below that benchmark. This is not sufficient to claim causal or generalizable biological effect, but it is a scientifically meaningful dataset-specific association. I therefore registered the reversed directional claim and accepted it provisionally on discovery evidence, while requesting independent validation of the same comparison through H45 to guard against multiplicity and sampling error. H47 is the closest remaining unresolved candidate: feature_028 level_001 versus level_003 on outcome_009 has estimate 0.0236, just below the 10% benchmark, with upper bound 0.0539, but the exposed cell is small and the point estimate is not yet clearly clinically meaningful. H43, H44, H46, and H55 have upper bounds that cross the approximate clinical threshold but point estimates far below it, so they are deferred as low-priority borderline screens. H18, H41, H42, H56, H57, and H58 have positive-claim upper bounds below their clinical thresholds or otherwise insufficient support in the claimed direction and are rejected/closed. H41 has a negative lower bound beyond threshold, but the point estimate in the opposite direction is only about 5% of the outcome mean, so I do not pursue a reversed follow-up now. The feature_034/feature_002 family remains deprioritized because H34 failed validation and outcome_014 estimates were unstable and directionally inconsistent. The main active hypothesis is now the reversed feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 association on outcome_007 pending validation.

No new independent validation response was due for H60/H45 in this synthesis. The accepted claim H60 remains supported in this supplied dataset: feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 is associated with outcome_007 raw difference about -0.0503 (signed +0.0503 for negative direction), about 20.5% of the absolute outcome_007 mean; interval is +0.0218 to +0.0788. This supports a stronger-dependency association in the dataset, but the lower bound is only slightly below the approximate 10% absolute benchmark and acceptance was discovery-only, so independent validation is now the priority. H45 is the corresponding positive claim and is closed because the observed signal is in the opposite direction. H60 remains active pending validation. Feature_034/feature_002 leads remain deprioritized because H34 failed validation and outcome_014 contrasts are unstable and directionally inconsistent. Many new screens are negative for clinically meaningful claimed effects (H18,H41,H42,H56,H57,H58 and earlier closed marginals). Unresolved borderline items remain (e.g., H47, H40/H43/H44/H46/H55-type upper bounds, H4 and H28/H35), but none should be promoted without independent confirmation. I deferred lower-priority outcome_013 categorical and rare-binary screens to make capacity for follow-up on the feature_009 lead. Proposed follow-ups test whether the effect is specific to the level_001-versus-level_003 contrast by comparing level_001 with level_002 and level_002 with level_003, and test whether similar feature_009 shifts appear in other dependency scores (outcome_013, outcome_001). I also registered high-prevalence binary screens on outcome_007 as context controls. These remain dataset-specific associations, not causal or generalizable claims. Next iteration should request independent validation of H60 before expanding feature_009 conclusions.

No validation response is due in this explore stage, and the only accepted finding remains H60: in this supplied dataset, feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 is associated with a lower outcome_007 dependency score (raw contrast about -0.050; signed +0.050 under the negative-direction claim), larger than the approximate 10% absolute benchmark for outcome_007 (~0.0245), although the discovery interval lower bound is slightly below that benchmark. The immediate priority is still to request independent validation of H60 in the next appraise stage. In parallel, I registered focused consistency checks for the same feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 contrast across other stable negative-mean dependency outcomes. These are linked to H60 with motivating evidence R44 and use direction -1 because the accepted association was that level_001 is more negative than level_003 on outcome_007; if the same stronger-dependency pattern appears elsewhere, the signed estimate will be positive and can be judged against the 10% absolute benchmark. These are not independent confirmations of generalizability; they are within-dataset specificity and coherence tests. I avoided feature_009 follow-up on outcome_014 and outcome_006 because their means are near zero, making relative 10% inference unstable. I also registered high-prevalence outcome_007 controls with feature_023, feature_054 level_002 versus level_001, and feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 to test whether outcome_007 shows widespread predictor associations or whether feature_009 is relatively specific. Existing active outcome_013 and outcome_001 feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 claims (H63/H64) and level_002 intermediate contrasts (H61/H62/H50) remain useful; I did not duplicate them. Finally, I deferred H12 and H27 to reduce wasted follow-up on the unstable feature_034/feature_002 outcome_014 family. All proposals remain dataset-specific association hypotheses and do not imply causality or biological generalizability.

I request 12 feature_009-focused comparisons that are currently untested. These are more scientifically urgent than additional broad screens because H60 is the only accepted finding so far and it concerns feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 on outcome_007. H61 and H62 test the intermediate level pattern on the outcome where the association was found: level_001 versus level_002 and level_002 versus level_003. These will distinguish a localized level_001 effect from a gradient or from a level_003-specific pattern. H63, H64, and H68-H75 test whether the same feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 contrast appears across other stable dependency-score outcomes with reasonably large absolute means. For H63 and H64 the registered direction is positive, so a raw negative association with level_001 would appear as a negative signed estimate; for H68-H75 the direction was chosen negative so that a raw lower dependency score in level_001 than in level_003 appears as a positive signed estimate. These comparisons are not independent confirmations of generalizability; they are within-dataset consistency and specificity checks. I avoided feature_009 follow-up on outcome_014 and outcome_006 because their near-zero means make relative 10% inference unstable. I deferred H50 and outcome_007 context controls H76-H78 because the highest-value question is whether the accepted feature_009 signal is specific to outcome_007 or broad across dependency scores, and whether level_002 is intermediate. All returned estimates will be interpreted as already signed to the registered claim direction and judged against approximately 10% of the outcome mean, with valid cell sizes required for each comparison.

The new feature_009 level-pattern tests are mostly uninformative or null. H61 and H62 cannot be interpreted because level_002 has only 13 observations, so I close them as unresolved/infeasible rather than as evidence of absence. H63 tests the same feature_009 level_001 vs level_003 contrast on outcome_013 with a positive claim direction. The signed estimate is +0.0185, below the roughly 0.027 absolute 10% benchmark, with a confidence interval crossing zero; it does not support a clinically meaningful positive association and the raw direction is not the H60 pattern, so H63 is rejected and closed. H64 tests the same contrast on outcome_001 with a positive claim direction. The signed estimate is -0.0808, i.e., a raw negative contrast, with interval [-0.1449, -0.0166]. This rejects the positive claim, but it reveals a large opposite raw association: level_001 has about 0.081 lower outcome_001 than level_003, roughly 19% of the absolute outcome_001 mean. Because the original claim direction was positive, H64 is rejected as a positive claim; I registered a reversed negative-direction refinement linked to H64. H68-H75 test the same feature_009 contrast across other stable dependency scores. Their signed estimates are small, cross zero, and in some cases point opposite the claimed direction; none provide meaningful support for a broad feature_009 association, so they are rejected/closed. The strongest remaining feature_009 evidence is therefore outcome-specific: H60 on outcome_007 and the newly observed raw pattern on outcome_001. Since multiplicity, rare-level imprecision, and lack of validation remain, I request independent validation of H60 first. If H60 validates, it anchors the feature_009 outcome_007 association; then the reversed outcome_001 claim should be considered for validation. If H60 fails validation, the feature_009 family should be substantially downgraded despite the outcome_001 signal.

The independent validation response changes the main conclusion: H60 is no longer supported. H60 originally accepted a feature_009 level_001 versus level_003 association with lower outcome_007 dependency (signed +0.0503, 95% Welch interval +0.0218 to +0.0788). Its independent validation estimate, however, is signed -0.0103 with interval -0.0511 to +0.0304. The validation interval crosses zero, the point estimate has the opposite sign, and its upper bound is far below the discovery point estimate. Because the discovery lower bound was already only just below the approximate 10% absolute benchmark for outcome_007 (~0.0245), and validation provides no corroboration, I reject H60 and close it. The best current reading is that H60 was a discovery-specific false positive or at least not a reproducible dataset association. This is not a claim of no biological effect; it is a claim that the supplied evidence no longer supports an accepted association. The corresponding positive claim H45 remains closed, and feature_009 cross-outcome tests did not support a broad pattern across other dependency scores. The only remaining feature_009 signal is H79 on outcome_001: signed +0.0808, interval +0.0166 to +0.1449 under the negative-direction claim. Its point estimate is large (~19% of the absolute outcome_001 mean), but the lower bound is below the 10% benchmark and, given H60's validation failure, this discovery-only signal is not strong enough to accept. H79 should be the next validation priority. If H79 independently validates, I would then use registered outcome_001 controls and feature_009 level contrasts to assess specificity and level pattern. If H79 fails validation, the feature_009 family should be substantially downgraded and the investigation should pivot to high-prevalence predictors with lower false-positive risk. The feature_034/feature_002 family is also closed: H34 validation is null, H28/H35 evidence is inconsistent with the claimed direction and null under validation, and related interactions are unstable. These rejections represent lack of supported association in this dataset, not proof of causal absence or generalizable null.

No assessments are due in this explore stage. The central scientific question is whether H79, outcome_001 with feature_009 level_001 versus level_003, is a real dataset association or another discovery-specific false positive analogous to H60. H79 has a large discovery point estimate, signed +0.0808 under the negative claim direction, but its lower bound falls below the approximate 10% benchmark and the exposed level is rare, so it should be validated rather than accepted. I did not duplicate the already active outcome_001 specificity controls H80-H87 or the outcome_007 controls H65-H78. To broaden exploration while reducing false-positive risk, I registered high-prevalence binary and categorical screens on outcome_008 and outcome_011, two relatively under-screened stable negative-mean dependency outcomes. Each comparison is registered with direction -1 to test whether the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e., stronger dependency. Because labels are opaque, anticipated direction is uncertain; large negative signed estimates would indicate an opposite raw contrast and could be followed by a reversed refinement if scientifically plausible. These new proposals also provide context for H79: if many high-prevalence predictors show large effects, a single rare feature_009 contrast is less compelling; if high-prevalence screens remain null and H79 independently validates, H79 becomes a more defensible outcome-specific association.

I selected currently untested claims that are most informative for the remaining lead, H79, while also adding high-power discovery screens. H80-H84 test whether outcome_001 has broader high-prevalence predictor associations or whether the rare feature_009 level_001 contrast in H79 is an isolated finding. H85-H87 test other feature_009 levels against level_003 on outcome_001, helping distinguish a level_001-specific signal from a general non-level_003 versus level_003 pattern. I did not rerun H79 because it already has discovery evidence and a repeated test would not provide a new sample; independent validation of H79 will be considered after these specificity checks and screens. H88-H91 test high-prevalence predictors on outcome_008, a stable negative-mean outcome with limited prior screening and a 10% benchmark of roughly 0.028. Outcome_008 was prioritized over outcome_011 for the initial high-prevalence set because its outcome mean is slightly smaller, giving a comparable threshold with reasonable power. All selected analyses are association hypotheses in the supplied dataset, not causal claims.

The 12 new discovery results mostly reduce the number of competing explanations for H79 while revealing one secondary borderline lead. For outcome_001, H80 and H81 are high-prevalence binary controls and are clinically and statistically null; their intervals are wide but centered near zero. H83 and H84 are also not clinically meaningful: H83 is positive but below the approx 0.0415 10% threshold, and H84 is negative and below threshold in magnitude. H82 is the most promising outcome_001 alternative: its signed estimate is +0.0514, about 12% of the absolute outcome_001 mean, but its interval crosses zero and is wide, so it is deferred rather than accepted or rejected. The feature_009 level-pattern controls on outcome_001 do not support a broad non-level_003 effect: H86 is null, while H85 and H87 are too rare and imprecise to be informative, so their investigations are closed. Thus the remaining feature_009 signal, if real, would be specific to level_001 versus level_003 on outcome_001, but H60's validation failure makes me cautious about accepting H79 without validation. For outcome_008, H88 is essentially exactly at the 10% benchmark (signed +0.0282) and H89 is slightly above it (signed +0.0322), with both intervals excluding zero but not excluding the clinical threshold. These are high-prevalence leads, but they are discovery-only and near the decision boundary, so they are deferred pending validation of the stronger primary lead. H90 and H91 are null and closed. I therefore request independent validation of H79. If H79 validates, it would be the strongest candidate dataset-specific association; if it fails, H89 and then H82 become the next validation priorities.

The new independent validation responses are decisive and lower the evidence quality of the prior lead. H79 (outcome_001, feature_009 level_001 vs level_003, negative-direction claim) had a discovery signed estimate of +0.0808 [0.0166, 0.1449], corresponding to a raw contrast about 19% of the absolute outcome_001 mean. However, its independent validation signed estimate is -0.0319 [-0.1149, 0.0510]: the point estimate reverses direction, the interval crosses zero, and even the upper bound is far below the discovery point. This does not support the H79 association. Given that H60, the analogous feature_009 outcome_007 association, also failed independent validation, the feature_009 rare-level family should be downgraded. H79 is therefore rejected and closed; no accepted feature_009 claim remains. H1 (outcome_001, feature_002 1 vs 0, negative-direction claim) also failed support: discovery was +0.0061 [-0.0260, 0.0383], and validation is +0.0354 [-0.0118, 0.0826]. The validation point is below the approximate 10% absolute-mean benchmark for outcome_001 (~0.0415), the interval includes zero, and the combined evidence does not justify accepting a clinically meaningful association. H1 remains rejected and closed. Current supported findings: none. Major negative findings: feature_009 level_001 vs level_003 associations are not reproducible for outcome_007 or outcome_001, feature_034/feature_002 family is closed, and many cross-outcome and specificity controls are null. Unresolved findings: H89 is the strongest remaining candidate, outcome_008 feature_008 1 vs 0, signed +0.0322 [0.0028, 0.0617], about 11.4% of the absolute outcome_008 mean, but its lower confidence bound is well below the 10% benchmark. H88 (outcome_008 feature_047) is almost exactly at threshold, signed +0.0282 [0.0019, 0.0546]. H82 (outcome_001 feature_023) has a large point estimate, signed +0.0514 [-0.0024, 0.1052], but is imprecise and crosses zero. Next analysis should prioritize independent validation of H89, with H88 and H82 as backups. The newly registered high-prevalence screens on outcome_008 and outcome_011 are intended to test whether these borderline leads are isolated or part of a broader high-prevalence predictor pattern. Future interpretation remains dataset-specific; these findings do not establish causality or generalizability.
